articles.title: Former Bond girl actress has no interest in her successor: ‘I don’t really care, guys’
articles.summary: Léa Seydoux laughed when asked which actress could take her place, and criticized the franchise: “It became American.”
articles.body:
French movie star and former Bond girl Léa Seydoux said she has no interest in whoever succeeds her in the franchise.

Seydoux admitted that she couldn't care less about who takes the reins opposite Robert Pattinson.

"I'm like, I don't really care, guys. How can you?" the No Time to Die star said.

A major ex-Bond girl does not, in fact, have her sights set on whoever succeeds her opposite Robert Pattinson in the next 007 movie .

Blue Is the Warmest Colour breakout and No Time to Die actress Léa Seydoux recently (and candidly) admitted that she has no interest in which actress next steps into the Bond girl role.

"Who do you think should be the next Bond girl? Or Bond woman?" the French star was asked on a new episode of The Run-Through podcast (below), tied to her role in the critically lauded Netflix drama Gentle Monster . The episode was recorded prior to Monday's announcement of Pattinson as the next Bond.

"I don't really care," the star said, laughing as she dismissed the thought. "I don't really care, guys. How can you?"

She went on to criticize the franchise's evolution over the years, after she starred as Bond girl Madeleine Swann in Daniel Craig's Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021).

"Now it's a new era. It became American," Seydoux said. "But I'm sure the movie will be great because it's directed by Denis Villeneuve, who's a very talented director. I'm sure he will do something great."

Though Pattinson's casting hadn't been announced when the podcast was recorded, Seydoux said she felt that "it's really difficult to cast James Bond, because you need to find an actor with a depth and with many layers, and I don't think that the young generation really has that."

Pattinson will be the seventh man to play Bond, following the likes of Craig, Pierce Brosnan, and more. Seydoux is part of a long lineage of women who've played iconic Bond girls.

Seydoux succeeded icons like Halle Berry, Michelle Yeoh, and Jane Seymour. Other past Bond girls include Denise Richards, Ana de Armas, Eva Green, Rosamund Pike, and more.

Following Monday's announcement, Pattinson expressed excitement in portraying 007 in the future.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

"James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime," the Twilight alum said in a statement, noting that he's "deeply grateful" for Amazon MGM Studios' "belief in me" to handle the role.

Listen to Seydoux discuss her Bond girl successor in the podcast episode above.

articles.title: How did 'I Play Rocky' star Anthony Ippolito transform into Sylvester Stallone? Raw eggs, a 40-pound weight gain and some X-rated homework.
articles.summary: Anthony Ippolito on bulking up for "I Play Rocky," finding Sylvester Stallone's voice in old footage and how he feels about fame.
articles.body:
Before raw eggs were part of a training montage, they were what Sylvester Stallone ate when he was broke. In his memoir, The Steps , he remembers getting by on spoonfuls of cottage cheese and three or four raw eggs as a struggling actor in New York. He couldn't afford the laundromat, so he'd get in the shower with his clothes on and wash everything at once.

That's the Stallone we meet in Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky , in theaters Nov. 20. He's still trying to make a living as an actor when he writes a script about a Philadelphia boxer who gets an unlikely shot at the heavyweight title. Hollywood wants the script, and Stallone could use the money. But he's willing to risk the whole movie to play the boxer himself.

Nearly 50 years later, Anthony Ippolito heard Farrelly was making a movie about how Stallone got his shot. So he went down to his grandma's basement on Long Island and made himself an audition tape, which he sent in unsolicited. Farrelly had been planning to look all over the world for his Stallone. After he saw the tape, he stopped searching.

Ippolito thought he'd have about six months to get in Stallone shape, he tells Yahoo. A production delay gave him closer to a year and a half, and he was glad to have it. He put on about 40 pounds, eating as much protein as he could every day.

I ask if there's anything he ate so often he never wants to see it again, and I'm a little surprised when he says he can't think of anything. "The diet was pretty nuts," he says, but he knew he'd be eating this way for a while. "Man, I gotta figure out a way to kind of enjoy this," he remembers thinking. "I'm gonna go crazy."

Grant Roberts, who'd worked with Stallone himself, came in about six months before shooting to help with the diet and put Ippolito through what the actor calls "pretty heavy lifting." Between that and his sessions with boxing choreographer Bobby Beckles, Ippolito was working out twice a day near the end of pre-production. He was also digging through old footage, trying to hear how Stallone sounded before people started doing impressions of him.

Ippolito had played a young Al Pacino in The Offer , about the making of The Godfather . Playing Stallone at a similar point in his career sent him to some less obvious places. He found the future superstar in Kojak and The Lords of Flatbush , and I have to ask whether he'd also gotten around to Stallone's appearance in The Party at Kitty and Stud's , the 1970 softcore film later known as Italian Stallion . He did, he admits. It was from the right period, he points out. He wanted to see "the safe parts of it" — and discovered it wasn't as racy as he'd imagined.

"They had plots back then," he adds with a laugh.

Sometimes he'd isolate Stallone's voice and just listen. He paid attention to how the facial paralysis Stallone has had since birth shaped the way he speaks. He'd listened to Stallone say as many different things as he could until he picked up on "a specific rhythm to how he speaks."

But what actually came out of Ippolito's mouth when he finally met Stallone? "'It's an honor to meet you,'" he theorizes. "I don't exactly remember." He remembers being nervous, though. After getting to know Stallone through whatever footage he could find, he could finally hear from the person who'd lived it. "This is his story," he says. "I was just ready to hear whatever he was willing to share."

Stallone did give him some advice, including "some stuff that I can't say." Ippolito will say that having Stallone in his corner "really did mean the world."

There's another tape of Ippolito I'd like to see. He was around 3 when his 40-mph fastball got him on Regis and Kelly . Does his mom still have the footage? "I hope," he says. "I gotta go dig it up." He kept playing baseball and acting as he grew up on Long Island, and he still can't pinpoint when one won out over the other. He was already acting when he got hurt playing baseball in college, and he happened to book a role in a series around the same time. "That kind of was a turning point," he says.

At 26, Ippolito says he likes to fish and is pretty sure he could quote The Sandlot from memory. He's a certified Gen Zer, but I decide he's an old soul when I ask about his first celebrity crush. "Marilyn Monroe," he says. "That sounds absurd, but it's just true."

He takes a little longer to answer when I ask about fame — he's playing one of Hollywood's biggest superstars in a movie with a lot of buzz , after all. He tells me he hasn't given it much thought. "It's nice to have people say kind things," he says, "but it's a very weird time. Like, the internet … oh, man."

The people he's sure about are the ones who already know him. "I'm very grateful that I have a close group of friends," he says, "people that this doesn't really have anything to do with."

articles.title: Bowen Yang Apologizes for Antisemitic Remark About Regina Spektor
articles.summary: Bowen Yang apologized Friday after facing criticism for referring to Jewish singer Regina Spektor as a an antisemitic slur, during an October episode of the...
articles.body:
Bowen Yang apologized Friday after facing criticism for referring to Jewish singer Regina Spektor as a "Zio," an antisemitic slur, during an October episode of the "Las Culturistas" podcast. But Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt criticized the apology, accusing the comedian of normalizing antisemitism and taking issue with a follow-up post in which Yang added, "At the same time, Free Palestine." In a Friday Instagram post, the "Saturday Night Live" alum said he had used the word without knowing its antisemitic history and acknowledged that he had adopted language popularized by far-right movements.

"I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we've repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks," Yang said in a Friday Instagram post . "Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against."

Later Friday, Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt responded to Yang's apology, saying the comedian had given the public a "textbook example of normalizing antisemitism."

"First, you breezily used the antisemitic slur 'Zio' on your show, got called out for it, and then issued a meager apology," he wrote in an X post . "You claimed not to know the history of the term, explaining you were upset to learn it was popularized by far-right white supremacists."

He continued: "Are you kidding me? The problem to you wasn't that you used an antisemitic slur; the problem was that you used the wrong one? Then you have the chutzpah to immediately follow up with a second post that reads, 'At the same time, Free Palestine.'"

"Seriously? Apologizing for your antisemitism with not one, but two qualifications isn't an apology at all," he concluded. "It was a reminder that you don't feel like Jews deserve the same respect as everyone else. That's not political speech; it's prejudice — and it's pathetic."

Greenblatt was not the only one to take issue with the apology. Many others criticized Yang's response, including lawyer Sarah Ettedgui, who posted on X about a comment she said she had left on his post that was later deleted.

"My comment was gaining traction," she said. "I challenged his reasoning and asked him to confront the antisemitism that has become normalized within his political circles. He deleted it."

In an Oct. 14 episode of "Las Culturistas," Yang and co-host Matt Rogers interviewed "Jury Duty" star Edy Modica. Spektor's name came up while the three were discussing SUNY Purchase, where the "Fidelity" singer attended college.

"And now she's out to lunch," Modica commented, prompting Rogers to ask the actress if she was "upset with Regina lately."

"She's just like a little Israel hardcore," Modica noted, as Yang chimed in: "Yeah, she's Zio."

"It's crazy. Someone like that. So crazy," the actress went on, sparking laughter from Yang and Rogers.

"Zio" is an antisemitic slur popularized by former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke.

Although the episode was posted more than a month ago, a clip of the conversation resurfaced on X this week, prompting several celebrities to condemn the comedian's word choice by Thursday.

"Bowen Yang using antisemitic slang that was popularized and mainstreamed by KKK leader David Duke is really just chefs kiss for the guy who got Shane Gillis fired from SNL for racism," Meghan McCain wrote on X Thursday evening. "Well done buying this hate mongering podcast @Disney." (Disney+ began streaming "Las Culturistas," an iHeart podcast, on November 18)

Actor Michael Rapaport also expressed his frustration with Yang and the conversation that took place on "Las Culturistas," writing on X, "These little hypocrites spend HOURS crying about the homophobia they've experienced, yet have ZERO problem being openly hostile, judgmental and dismissive toward JEWS."

"'Zio' is an antisemitic slur popularized by David Duke, now being normalized on the far left & far right," Amy Spitalnick, CEO of the Jewish Council for Public Affairs wrote as the clip went viral. "It's incredibly disappointing that Bowen Yang used it to refer to Regina Spektor, a Jewish artist. He can take this as an opportunity to engage on antisemitism—I hope he will."

For more reactions to Yang's remarks click here .

articles.title: Prince Harry shares how kids are adjusting to life in UK
articles.summary: Prince Harry says Archie and Lilbet are gaining confidence as they adjust to British schools.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Prince Harry says his two children are gaining confidence and gradually losing their American accents as they adjust to life in the United Kingdom after moving from California earlier this year.

During an appearance Friday on ITV's " This Morning, " the Duke of Sussex discussed how Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, are adapting to British schools.

Harry described the transition as a major cultural adjustment, particularly when it comes to wearing school uniforms, something the children were not accustomed to in California.

"The confidence in both of them has gone through the roof since being at a U.K. school, which is really, really nice," Harry said.

When asked whether his children still have American accents, Harry joked that he was working to change that.

"I'm squeezing the accents out of them and their friends at school are doing the same," Harry said.

Harry also joked about the difference between American and British vocabulary, saying his children understand the word "candy" better than the British term "sweets."

Harry and Meghan , the Duchess of Sussex, returned to the UK with their children in August after spending about six years in California following their decision to step back from royal duties in 2020.

During the interview, Harry reflected on his return to Britain, saying the country still feels like home.

He also said he missed the changing seasons while living in California, particularly British winters.

The interview came days after Harry and Meghan attended a holiday fair in London with Archie and Lilibet, marking the family's first public outing together since returning to Britain.

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence, 36, Shows Off Her “New” Breast Implants on Live TV
articles.summary: “It’s a full C.”
articles.body:
Jennifer Lawrence appeared on Watch What Happens Live on November 19, where she revealed she had gotten breast implants.

"I have implants…they're new," she said.

The 36-year-old actress also shared the name and location of her surgeon.

Jennifer Lawrence shared her latest cosmetic procedure on the November 19 episode of Watch What Happens Live .

While discussing Bravo hot takes with host Andy Cohen , the 36-year-old actress revealed, "I have implants…they're new." She then extended her chest forward and turned in her chair to show them off. "Dr. Teitelbaum in Santa Monica," she added, referring to her surgeon.

"Are those Bs?" Cohen asked about her bra cup size.

"No, it's a full C," Lawrence replied. "I think. It's the same size that they were."

Lawrence's comments come weeks after she said she wants a facelift someday.

"I want to be a sexy mom," she told The Cut on October 27. "At drop-off, I want to look like a woman that has her shit together even when I've just woken up and don't have my shit together." Lawrence shares two children with her husband, Cooke Maroney .

In a September Vogue interview , the Oscar winner shared her thoughts on various other cosmetic procedures and said she currently gets "baby Botox."

"Yeah, because I can't really get very much done," she said. "I need to have movement in my face—I get baby Botox, but I can't do a lot. If my skin is going to be a little saggier than I would like, at least it looks dewy and pretty."

She also said she's on a "retinol journey" and shared her Tretinoin tips. "Well, you have to sandwich . You have to use night cream, like something really moisturizing. Then Tret. Then a spritz of water and oil, because what I didn't realize for so long, and I'm really happy to tell you this: Oil traps the water in, so you have to give oil some water that the oil sits on top of so that it seals it into your skin."

The Hunger Games star also got candid about the one procedure she's against. "Oh, I'm really nervous about these fat transfers," she said. "I support other people doing them because I want to continue to watch and see what happens, but I don't know about that."

"I mean, I would love to have a buccal fat removal," she added. "I can't because everybody would know, but just know that I want that."

articles.title: Iza analisa fase mais vulnerável em novo álbum: 'Estou mais livre pra errar na frente dos outros' | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora lança 'ZAZA', projeto que vem acompanhado de um filme. Ao g1, artista falou sobre o 3º álbum, e comentou críticas sobre investir mais tempo em publicidade do que na música.
articles.summary: Cantora lança 'ZAZA', projeto que vem acompanhado de um filme. Ao g1, artista falou sobre o 3º álbum, e comentou críticas sobre investir mais tempo em publicidade do que na música.
articles.body:
Três anos após "Afrodhit", Iza chega com seu terceiro álbum. ZAZA, um disco com inspirações de reggae, reflete também uma nova fase da cantora: mais leve e "mais livre para errar na frente dos outros".

O relato foi feito pela própria artista em entrevista ao g1 , dias antes da chegada de ZAZA ao mundo. O álbum de 13 músicas ainda veio acompanhado de um filme de cerca uma hora. O tipo de projeto tem se tornado tendência no mercado. Gaby Amarantos fez isso em "Rock Doido". Anitta, com "Equilibrivm". E o formato chega em uma fase em que os artistas deixaram de investir milhões em videoclipes.

"O natural é que você, hoje em dia, fazendo clipe, pague muito mais e que menos pessoas vejam. Para o investimento, é uma coisa que acaba não fazendo sentido. Eu gastei nesse vídeo, nesse filme, o que eu gastaria em um clipe", aponta Iza.

No bate-papo, Iza também falou sobre a demora para o lançamento de ZAZA, citou as mudanças que sua filha, Nala, de 2 anos, trouxe para sua vida e carreira, e analisou as críticas de que teria investido mais tempo fazendo publicidade do que músicas.

"Eu entendo, eu super entendo, porque eu acho que as pessoas acabam colocando a gente em algumas caixas e comparando. As pessoas enxergam, sei lá, um produto que está aqui lançando 12 músicas por ano, e eu que estou lançando duas. Eu continuo lançando músicas, eu só lanço menos. Mas as pessoas acreditam talvez que eu tenha deixado de lado."

Capa do álbum 'Zaza', de Iza — Foto: Divulgação

g1 - Pra começar, eu queria esmiuçar um pouquinho a carta que você escreveu antes do lançamento. Em um trecho dela, você fala que ficou muito tempo escondida. Por que você foi para esse esconderijo e o que te tirou de lá para lançar esse álbum? Iza - A Nala me tirou desse esconderijo. E acho que fiquei muito escondida porque me surpreendi com o quanto a internet pode fazer parte da nossa vida. Eu só quero falar aqui nessa entrevista sobre coisas que interessam e que merecem atenção, porque tem coisas que não merecem atenção.

Mas é inevitável dizer que nos últimos dois anos eu experimentei algo que eu nunca tinha experimentado antes e isso foi um alerta, sabe? E eu precisei me esconder mesmo e meio que recalibrar a minha relação com a rede social, o que fazia sentido para mim, o que era saudável, quando era interessante trazer a minha filha ou não.

Então acho que eu falo um pouco disso quando digo que fico muito tempo escondida. E também estou analisando a minha carreira inteira. Faço dez anos de carreira esse ano. E eu acredito que me escondi muito atrás dessa capa, essa couraça de empoderamento e perfeição que acabam cobrando de nós mulheres.

g1 - Você sempre foi um símbolo de empoderamento, mas quando teve momentos de vulnerabilidade, acabou sendo julgada. Qual o peso de ser, digamos, a rainha do empoderamento? Iza - Eu aprendi que o peso é o peso que eu dou para isso. No início da minha carreira, talvez por ser uma mulher preta e por ter conquistado coisas que nunca imaginei conquistar, eu sempre ficava assim: 'não, calma, vamos devagar aqui, vamos pisar muito em ovos e fazer tudo com muito cuidado. Porque se eu falar isso, a pessoa pode se ofender'. E aí você vai virando robô.

E tudo bem se essa fosse uma intenção, mas no momento que você quebra, no momento que você escorrega, as pessoas levam um susto.

Tenho procurado reiterar cada vez mais a narrativa de que eu sou uma pessoinha. E é meio tosco falar isso: 'eu sou só uma pessoa'. Mas é assim, porque acho que as pessoas veem a gente com uma distância muito grande, e têm acesso só às coisas que eu dou. E com esses fragmentos, elas constroem uma personalidade inteira. E eu sou muito mais do que isso.

Eu sou muitas luzes e muitas sombras também. E abraçar essas sombras me dá um pouco de paz, porque você não fica esperando que os outros não enxerguem essas sombras. Faz parte de mim e pronto.

g1 - Está mais livre para ser vulnerável? Iza – Uhum. Estou mais livre pra errar na frente dos outros.

g1 - Na carta você também fala que perdeu o controle da sua narrativa. Isso é algo que acontece muito com pessoas perfeccionistas, esse medo de perder esse controle. Então você é uma pessoa perfeccionista? Iza - Eu sou muito perfeccionista. E muito controladora também. E eu acho que isso tem a ver com ansiedade. Quanto mais ansiosa você é, mais controladora você se torna, para que você consiga pelo menos tentar mediar as suas sensações.

Então acho que tentei prever muita coisa, adiantar soluções. E também, sem querer, com muito medo de desagradar, de perder um lugar que eu conquistei com o meu trabalho, como se esse lugar fosse frágil. Eu sinto que esse controle me adoeceu.

Soltar as rédeas, ainda que de forma forçada, foi uma das melhores coisas que tinha acontecido na minha vida, porque você vê que a vida continua, que a vida segue.

g1 - Tem um trecho que me chama a atenção na carta em que você cita que conheceu a sua sombra. Logo depois você emenda que você deixou a luz entrar. Essa sombra tem relação com o que você acabou de falar e que te fez adoecer? É o buraco em que às vezes a gente se encontra? Iza

É, eu acho que foi o buraco que eu me enfiei. (risos) E lá estava bom de escuro. Eu acho que foi isso. Quando eu falo sobre sombras, eu falo das partes de mim e da minha história que eu tenho vergonha ou que eu tinha vergonha e que foram expostas.

Eu acho que falo sobre uma vulnerabilidade muito grande que acabou transbordando sem que eu planejasse. Estava planejando o contrário. Acho que tentei controlar uma narrativa e, de repente, me vi no meio de um mar turbulento.

E quando eu falo que deixei a luz entrar, estou fazendo uma brincadeira, porque também é o nome de uma das músicas, mas estou falando da minha filha, e do quanto ela veio para me curar. Depois que você é mãe, entende que tudo o que você fazia antes era muito fácil.

Ser mãe é a parte mais difícil. É uma parte muito gostosa, mas é a parte mais difícil. Então, a Nala trouxe uma leveza muito grande para algo que antes era uma dor de cabeça, como a opinião dos outros, por exemplo.

Iza faz feats com seis artistas ao longo das 13 faixas do álbum 'Zaza' — Foto: Divulgação

g1 - Você já comentou que levou o tempo que precisou para fazer ZAZA. Mas muita gente criticou exatamente essa demora. Foram três anos que você ficou produzindo. Como você leva essas críticas? E como foi todo esse processo de produção? Iza - Para o meu segundo álbum ["Afrodhit", lançado em 2023], eu talvez tenha deixado essa pressão entrar. E eu também demorei quatro anos para lançar depois de "Dona de Mim".

O meu primeiro álbum nasceu sem querer. Comecei a fazer música, fiz várias. Eu não sabia que estava fazendo um álbum, então foi muito fácil fazer porque eu não tinha pressão de estar fazendo álbum.

O segundo, eu me senti pressionada pelo meu álbum de estreia, porque ele foi um grande sucesso. Então, você fica insegura, sabe? E acho que quanto mais você se torna inseguro na hora de criar, mais você procrastina.

E esse terceiro álbum, na verdade, está nascendo na hora certa, porque a Nala está fazendo 2 anos agora. Esse primeiro ano de maternidade é uma loucura. Eu estava tentando me ajustar, tentando voltar para mim.

Acho que ZAZA nasceu até rápido demais. A Nala já me ensinou muito sobre tempo, então já estou pensando no próximo trabalho. Sinto que não tenho tempo para perder, porque, como eu disse, difícil mesmo é ser mãe. Agora fazer álbum está ficando cada vez mais fácil, estou pegando o jeito.

g1 - Você lançou três músicas de reggae antes do álbum completo, só que elas não estão no ZAZA. Por que elas ficaram ali fora? Iza - "Caos e Sal", "Tão Bonito" e "Eu e Você" são músicas que têm tudo a ver com essa estética, são músicas de reggae. Mas eu queria trazer um trabalho inédito. Acho que isso ia tornar o álbum mais interessante.

E também achei que elas já não faziam parte da sonoridade que eu queria trazer no álbum. As músicas do álbum foram gravadas ao vivo, os músicos tocavam os instrumentos ao vivo. E estas três não foram feitas assim. Então, também por isso elas não entraram nesse álbum.

Cantora maranhense Núbia participa de novo álbum de IZA — Foto: Reprodução/ Ascom

g1 - Para compor esse álbum, você fez pela primeira vez um camping. Como que foi esse processo? Iza - Eu já tinha a Nala. E o ideal é que você realmente crie uma imersão, que você viaje com as pessoas, que você fique ali, tome café da manhã com as pessoas, crie uma rotina com elas, porque as ideias vão surgindo assim, no dia a dia. Só que eu não podia me ausentar assim, eu não ia conseguir viajar, ficar seis dias fora.

Então a gente alugou uma casa muito próxima da minha, que eu sabia que podia chegar na minha casa em cinco minutos. E fiquei lá durante esses seis dias internada com os músicos e os produtores. Foi muito especial.

Eu não cheguei lá com uma meta. A minha ideia era fazer uma música por dia. A gente fazia muito mais do que isso. E eu tava feliz, porque no final do camping não é garantido que você vá gostar de tudo que você fez. As músicas precisam amadurecer bem. Então eu fico feliz que deu certo, e que eu me dou muito bem com as pessoas que fizeram parte. Foi tudo muito gostoso.

g1 - O álbum vem acompanhado de um filme, que é algo que tem se tornado uma tendência no mercado em um momento em que ninguém mais queria investir em um videoclipe, por exemplo, por ser algo muito caro. Vale a pena esse investimento em um filme? Iza - Eu entendo muito que hoje em dia a indústria mudou bastante. Em 2017, quando lancei "Pesadão", não existia Reels no Instagram, não existia TikTok pra gente. Então, se você quisesse ver uma pessoa se mexendo, você tinha que ir pra um lugar específico. As coisas não eram pulverizadas.

Era muito mais fácil uma marca, por exemplo, querer investir em um videoclipe porque a gente já sabia que as visualizações iam acontecer.

Se rolasse investimento de um clipe bonito, não estou falando nem de marketing, se o clipe fosse bonito, gerasse discussão, as pessoas iam assistir. Porque era ali naquela plataforma que as pessoas viam o vídeo exclusivamente. Hoje não. As redes sociais estão cada vez mais misturadas, e as coisas estão cada vez mais caras.

Então, o natural é que você, hoje em dia, fazendo clipe, pague muito mais e que menos pessoas vejam. Para o investimento, é uma coisa que acaba não fazendo sentido.

Eu gastei nesse filme, o que eu gastaria em um clipe. E é óbvio que você pode gastar o que você quiser, mas essa foi a minha ideia. E o clipe já é caríssimo. O que eu gastei para fazer esse vídeo foi muito parecido também com o que eu gastei para fazer o show do The Town. Não gosto de ficar falando de valores, mas é muito dinheiro.

Acho que hoje o desafio é a gente fazer um trabalho, criar um legado, e não enlouquecer também, porque não faz sentido enlouquecer. Eu sempre gostei muito de audiovisual. Eu acho que eu sempre fui uma artista que se dedicou muito a isso.

Tenho muito orgulho dos meus trabalhos, dos meus clipes, porque eu sei que alguns deles marcaram e são muito bonitos e bem trabalhados. Então, eu quis fazer uma coisa diferente do que eu já tinha feito. Dez anos de carreira e saiu o primeiro DVD.

Iza se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Miguel Folco/g1

g1 - Você falou da relação com as marcas e muitas pessoas fazem críticas citando que você ficou mais focada em fazer propaganda do que música. O que acha desse tipo de comentário? Iza - Eu super entendo, porque eu acho que as pessoas acabam colocando a gente em algumas caixas e comparando.

As pessoas enxergam, sei lá, um produto que está aqui lançando 12 músicas por ano, e eu que estou lançando duas. Eu continuo lançando músicas, eu só lanço menos. Mas as pessoas acreditam talvez que eu tenha deixado de lado.

E também acho que isso é muito reflexo de como o meu trabalho acabou impactando a vida das pessoas. Meu trabalho acabou acontecendo muito mais do que eu estava imaginando e muito mais do que eu conseguia sustentar, talvez, de primeira.

Quando eu lancei "Pesadão", nunca imaginei que as pessoas fossem gostar. Aí eu falei, vou lançar "Ginga": "Agora vão me achar doida". E as pessoas gostaram. Falei: "vou lançar 'Dona De Mim' no carnaval, ninguém vai entender nada". E as pessoas gostaram. Então, acho que você vai criando uma demanda também.

As pessoas estão aí para comentar, para falar, sabe? E ver isso com lucidez é muito bom. Mas é isso. Não sucumbindo a essa pressão, eu sinto que está no meu momento de acelerar mais essa produção. Porque agora está mais fácil mesmo. Agora eu já entendi como é que eu faço.

g1 - Hoje você já aceita mais que as pessoas vão gostar do seu trabalho? Iza - Hoje eu não vou ficar surpreendida se as pessoas gostarem. Porque ser artista é um negócio muito doido. Se você for um artista que está ali procurando fazer um trabalho e ser ovacionado, você vai ser um artista muito triste, uma pessoa muito triste.

Se esse for o seu tesão, o seu motor, você está colocando o seu tesão em uma coisa que você não pode controlar.

Eu tenho que fazer minha música pensando em mim. E isso é uma grande maluquice. Você trabalha com o público, mas você faz uma música para você e reza para que o público goste. É uma equação meio doida.

g1 - Você falou que faz música para você. E, no processo de divulgação, você comentou em um vídeo que não se vê mais cantando as músicas do álbum "Afrodhit". Elas vão sair do seu repertório? IZA - Eu vou continuar cantando. É a primeira vez que eu me exponho desse jeito nas redes sociais, falando coisas, e pensando. Ali eu estava trocando ideia com uma equipe.

E as pessoas ficaram: "É o quê? Você está maluca? Vai dormir que passa, amanhã é outro dia".

E eu entendo muito o que as pessoas estão falando. Eu não vou deixar de cantar as músicas de "Afrodhit" de jeito nenhum. O que eu quis dizer, naquela frase, é que o que eu estava sentindo naquele momento, gravando, já se esvaiu, porque eu fiz a música. A música fez com que eu desabafasse, e aí passou.

E agora, quando eu vou cantar a música, eu fico, gente, mas por que ela estava tão brava? O que aconteceu?

As músicas acabaram virando outras coisas para as pessoas que me seguem. e

Iza confirma o lançamento do terceiro álbum de estúdio na Semana da Consciência Negra, em novembro — Foto: Reprodução / X Iza

g1 - Você era uma IZA naquele álbum e que foi transbordado ali. E agora, quem é a Iza de Zaza? Iza - Ah, eu acho que é uma Iza mais de boa, uma Iza mais tranquila, mais pé no chão também, mais terapeutizada, mais feliz com o trabalho.

Tenho mais noção de como funcionam as coisas. Tenho colocado a minha expectativa nos lugares certinhos e continuo me surpreendendo.

Estou feliz com tudo que está sendo criado, feliz que é um trabalho pessoal, imperfeito, e que nasce de uma vontade grande de fazer e não de me encaixar no mercado. E isso para a gente que é artista é ouro.

g1 - Ouvindo o álbum, na hora que eu ouvi "Girassol", achei que ela representa a sua nova fase. Viajei muito? Iza - Viajou zero. "Girassol" termina o álbum exatamente por isso. É importante que seja a última música, porque é o recado que eu quero dar, que hoje ela já não chora mais, depois de tanto tempo o sol se abriu, balançou, mas ancorou no cais, foi dado o tempo ao tempo, o jardim floresceu, encontrou a paz, e o que aconteceu já ficou para trás.

É o recado que eu quero deixar para o mundo, é assim que eu tenho me sentido agora.

articles.body:
Uma música pode ficar gravada na memória por conta da letra, da melodia, do ritmo... e também do sabor!

A segunda edição do Festival Botecar em Juiz de Fora tem como tema "Os sabores que tocam a gente" e reúne 25 bares que se inspiraram na música para criar petiscos e conquistar o público. Veja, a seguir, a lista completa dos pratos.

Entre as inspirações estão artistas que nasceram em Juiz de Fora e ganharam projeção nacional, como Ana Carolina , referência para três receitas , e as bandas Strike e Onze:20.

Na lista estão também ícones nacionais que mantêm uma relação especial com a cidade, como é o caso de Milton Nascimento e João Bosco .

Também há aqueles que já fazem parte da identidade cultural juiz-forana, como é o caso do tradicional grupo Bacharéis do Samba, o bloco carnavalesco Só Love e o sambista Mamão , nome artístico de Armando Fernandes de Aguiar, compositor dos clássicos "Tristeza Pé no Chão" e " Princesinha de Minas", que inspirou três pratos .

Criado em Belo Horizonte, em 2014, o Festival Botecar se consolidou no calendário gastronômico e cultural mineiro e expandiu sua atuação para diferentes cidades brasileiras.

Em Juiz de Fora, a primeira edição foi realizada em 2025 e teve o Incite Beer como grande vencedor, com o petisco Herança Mineira . Além da experiência gastronômica, o festival pretende movimentar a economia local, com impacto no faturamento dos bares, na cadeia de fornecedores e na geração de oportunidades de trabalho.

Em 2026, o Botecar também será realizado em outras cidades, como Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Rio de Janeiro, Goiânia, Pouso Alegre, Divinópolis, Poços de Caldas, Uberlândia e Montes Claros.

articles.body: 'O.M: Operation Mole' has opened its theatrical run on a promising note, registering good numbers across domestic and international markets. The Tamil action crime thriller, featuring Mammootty, Dhanush and Sai Pallavi, collected Rs 17.70 cr in India net earnings on Friday, November 20. Its domestic gross collection stood at Rs 20.55 cr. The movie recorded 6,628 shows across its Tamil, Telugu and Hindi versions. This accounted for 75.4% of its total India net earnings. The Telugu version secured Rs 4 cr from 1,615 shows, contributing 22.6% to the domestic net collection. Meanwhile, the Hindi version added Rs 35 lakh through 990 shows, accounting for the remaining 2%.Across all three language versions, the movie registered an overall theatre occupancy of 45.6%.'O.M: Operation Mole' worldwide collection and overseas performanceInternational territories contributed Rs 11 cr, while the Indian theatrical market generated Rs 20.55 cr in gross earnings. Domestic markets accounted for 65.1% of the worldwide collection, with overseas territories contributing 34.9%.The Tamil 2D version recorded an overall occupancy of 56.21%. Morning screenings registered 45.23%, while afternoon shows improved to 50.85%. Evening occupancy reached 56.23%, before climbing to 72.54% during night shows.The Telugu 2D version registered an overall occupancy of 48.95%. Morning shows recorded 34.18%, followed by 41.09% in the afternoon and 38.64% in the evening. Night screenings witnessed the highest occupancy for this version at 60.91%.In comparison, the Hindi 2D version recorded an overall occupancy of 11.70%. articles.summary: Who will take pole position for the Las Vegas Grand Prix?
articles.body:
George Russell led the way in the third and final hour of practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Friday evening.

But will the Mercedes driver top the timing sheets during the all-important qualifying hour later tonight?

Russell led teammate Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris in FP3 Friday evening, with the veteran Mercedes driver posting a lap of 1:34.041, almost a full second ahead of Antonelli, who was 0.911 seconds off the pace. Charles Leclerc and Franco Colapinto rounded out the top five.

Friday's FP3 session was the only representative session of the weekend so far, as both FP1 and FP2 on Thursday were compromised by wet weather.

The biggest story so far in Las Vegas might just be the list of drivers taking a grid penalty due to new components. Five drivers — Antonelli, Lance Stroll, Oliver Bearman, Oscar Piastri, and Carlos Sainz — have already taken on new components ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix and are facing grid drops at the start of the race. Antonelli is facing a five-place grid drop, while Stroll, Piastri, and Sainz are facing ten-place grid drops.

Bearman, who is taking on a fifth Internal Combustion Engine, turbocharger, exhaust, and MGU-K, and as those components all exceed the permitted amount per season, he will start at the back of the grid.

But who will take pole position? We will find out soon enough. articles.body: Salman Khan makes it clear he will not lock horns with Shah Rukh Khan at the box office, as he explains why his war drama 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace' is arriving on December 4. articles.title: After missing Deva's funeral, Ilaiyaraaja pays tribute to the late composer at his posthumous birthday event; heartwarming gesture wins fans' hearts
articles.summary: Music maestro Ilaiyaraaja paid a heartfelt tribute to the late composer Deva, highlighting their long association and the mutual respect they shared for
articles.body: Music maestro Ilaiyaraaja paid a heartfelt tribute to the late composer Deva, highlighting their long association and the mutual respect they shared for each other's musical journeys. The veteran composer attended an event organised to mark Deva's posthumous birthday and offered flowers to his portrait. Pictures and videos from the event have since touched music lovers, with many appreciating Ilaiyaraaja's presence and his gesture towards the late composer.Ilaiyaraaja attends Deva's birthday celebrationIlaiyaraaja's appearance at the event comes weeks after questions were raised about his absence from Deva's funeral. The composer had earlier explained that he finds it difficult to see people close to him after their death. His decision not to attend the final rites had drawn criticism on social media, with some questioning whether personal differences had kept him away. However, his presence at the birthday event has now offered a different picture. articles.title: The British Indian filmmaker embracing two cultures on screen
articles.summary: Parvinder Shergill talks about creating art that honours both of her cultural backgrounds.
articles.body:
It was Hollywood more than Bollywood that British Indian filmmaker Parvinder Shergill grew up on, with Karate Kid, Rocky, A Few Good Men and ET among her favourite films.

The actor, writer and producer, who lives in Berkshire, says she feels "really lucky" that she comes from "two worlds".

Shergill says she builds stories around both cultures, the latest of which are her new film Touché and her first play Threads of Healing.

As she talks about wanting to "inspire" with her work, she says "it's an exciting time to embrace who you are, whatever that means to you".

Shergill says a lot of the work she consumed growing up was "very male-driven, global, mainstream, commercial".

But even though she wants to make work for the Western audience, she says her perspective "has an added layer of always having a female South Asian protagonist".

"I'm also going to be doing a sci-fi next year, there happens to be a brown woman in it, but it's not about her being brown. It's just she's in the sci-fi world."

She says she considers having a perspective from two cultures "a blessing".

"My sister does polo, I've done fencing and chess but we're British Indian women in a sari - that's wicked."

Shergill says the world of Bollywood world as "very visual, it's very culture rich, it's very high on emotions".

In contrast she says "especially [in] Britain, our work is very deep thinking, it's very articulate, it's very heavy on the words".

She says she has projects in the pipeline that will "honour both worlds in a global audience".

"I think there is a way to combine great emotion and visual storytelling the way Bollywood does, especially with the soundtracks, but with excellent writing and what British playwrights and screenwriters have to offer."

Her approach is through subtlety, such as making sure the accents of her characters reflect the area they are from.

"Instead of drinking tea she might drink chai or instead of wearing a simple studded earring it might be a beautiful intricate Indian earring.

"Once you make it normal, it's normal for the audience."

Shergill, who is also an NHS psychiatrist, says exploring mental health "will always be in all of my work".

Her play for BBC Radio 4 Drama , also available in print, explores personal trauma and overcoming it - a topic which she says is "really stigmatised still" in the South Asian community.

"It's a very difficult conversation and it's something I really try to look at."

She says trauma in all its forms is something that especially women in the community do not come forward with because they fear the consequences.

Bend It Like Beckham star Parminder Nagra plays the lead in Threads of Healing, which Shergill describes as "such a 360 moment".

"And Meera Syal, who plays her mother, I thought, 'we really look up to them in the community, hopefully people will listen and it will come more of a conversation piece'," she added.

Dame Meera has spoken openly about having been sexually harassed and assaulted.

On Touché, which will be screened in cinemas from 27 November, Shergill says she has "a soft place".

The film tells the story of a British South Asian woman named Deep, played by Shergill, who seeks to change her life by taking up fencing.

The actress had fenced in school and at university and describes it as "a mix of chess with pilates and yoga and weights".

"We were meant to get stunts and cranes and a stunt double but the ironic thing is, I could not find a stunt double who looked like me.

"That was just wild to me, so I thought, 'right, this is another reason to make the film'."

She says she "couldn't believe the cast we got", including Harry Potter star Matthew Lewis, comedian Paul Chowdhry and writer and actor Stephen Fry.

Shergill says there is also "an underlying mental storyline that I've dedicated the film to my grandfather who passed this year for that".

Of her own role she says it was inspired by the theme of the underdog who becomes a hero "but it happens to not be a boy [but] someone that looks like me and other women".

"I really wanted to make something where girls can look at and be like, 'you know what? I can be a good person despite what happens in life if I just try really hard', so I wanted it to be an inspiring story," she says.

The film won the Tongues on Fire Flame Award at the 28th UK Asian Film Festival and Shergill says she is now "really excited" for her "first ever theatrical release".

"We actually had a little South Asian boy who's now fencing, which is so cool, so you don't know how you can inspire people."

articles.title: Pankaj Tripathi says, 'I will put forward the concerns of filmmakers' on his role as a CBFC member and backs scrapping of Tatkal certification: 'You cannot expect the certification process to be completed in five hours'
articles.summary: Pankaj Tripathi, who joined the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) as a member two months ago, has spoken about the board's new rules that have
articles.body: Pankaj Tripathi, who joined the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) as a member two months ago, has spoken about the board's new rules that have created a stir in the film industry. He says the aim is to make certification smoother and bring filmmakers closer to the board.What has changed at CBFCSince Pankaj Tripathi came on board, the CBFC has brought in a few notable guidelines. Producers must now submit the full, finished version of their film, and a title will not be treated as final until the certificate is issued. The board can also ask for changes to it.Pankaj Tripathi on bridging the gapAfter attending a recent meeting, the actor said the board wants to be closer to creators. He told MidDay, “I came to know that the CBFC wants to reduce the gap between filmmakers and itself. Intelligent filmmakers know how to make movies, keeping in mind the country they cater to, and the board wants to understand the filmmakers. As a member, I’m still learning about how things work. Whenever I am called for a meeting, I will put forward the concerns of filmmakers."Why controversies get amplifiedThe CBFC has often landed in disputes over the years. Pankaj Tripathi stated that he feels the massive reach of cinema is the reason such issues grow so quickly. He said, “Films are a popular medium in India. Everything gets discussed and dissected quickly. Several people [on the board] watch the film. If there is a problem, it is to be discussed further. As artistes and filmmakers, we have to be mindful [of what we’re clearing], and to do so, diverse groups of people need to watch a film and [voice] their view at the certification level.”Support for ending Tatkal certificationFor the same reason, he supports the withdrawal of the Tatkal certification facility, which had come into force in June 2026. According to him, a decision this important needs careful examination at several levels. Pankaj Tripathi asserted, “The process of making a film takes months. You cannot expect the certification process to be completed in five hours. The members have responsibilities; they have to look at the objectives and guidelines.”When the CBFC was reconstitutedThe new 18-member body is chaired by Shashi Shekhar Vempati. Its members include Suniel Shetty, Preity Zinta, Priyadarshan, Prosenjit and Ricky Kej, among others.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.standfirst: La cantante ya habló en la alfombra roja de “un momento delicado” en España
articles.summary: La cantante ya habló en la alfombra roja de “un momento delicado” en España
articles.body: A nueve días de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, Rosalía protagonizó el momento más político de LOS40 Music Awards Santander 2026. La gala, celebrada este viernes en el Palau Sant Jordi de Barcelona, la coronó como gran triunfadora con cuatro premios. Antes de la gala, ya en la alfombra roja, la cantante había dejado una primera reflexión sobre la cita con las urnas. Preguntada por lo que puede pasar tras el 29-N, respondió: "Bueno, yo creo que es verdad que es un momento delicado y ojalá que todo vaya mejor, porque hace falta, yo creo". Después, vestida de negro y sola en el escenario, fue la encargada de entregar el premio especial Fenómeno Cultural del Año a Guitarricadelafuente. Antes de nombrarlo, leyó un discurso que no pasó desapercibido. "Cuando los tiempos son convulsos y tanto es cuestionado, películas como 'La bola negra' son más necesarias que nunca", arrancó. "Nos recuerdan que hubo figuras como Lorca, que a través de su poesía expresó algo tan difícil de expresar en su época. Precisamente por eso, hoy en día hay derechos conseguidos que hay que seguir defendiendo", añadió. Rosalía continuó con una frase dirigida al homenajeado: "Hay muchos sebastianes en este mundo y Guitarricadelafuente les da voz a todos ellos". Una referencia que conectaba con la actuación del artista minutos antes, en la que cantó colgado de un tronco y rodeado de flechas, evocando el martirio de San Sebastián. Finalmente, anunció el galardón "por su canción 'La nieve' y su interpretación en 'La bola negra'", la película que protagoniza el músico. No fue el único mensaje con lectura social. Alaska recibió un Golden Award por abrir espacio a la diversidad en una España muy distinta a la actual, y el Palau coreó 'A quién le importa' hasta detener la música. Aun así, el alegato de Rosalía, sin mencionar partidos ni pedir el voto, fue el más explícito en plena campaña electoral.

articles.title: Attempted murder charge over Bradford councillor stabbing
articles.summary: Arfan Ali is due before magistrates charged over Thursday's attack on Bradford councillor Ibrar Ali.
articles.body:
A man has been charged with attempted murder after a Bradford councillor was seriously injured in a stabbing.

Councillor Ibrar Ali was attacked at about 11:00 GMT on Thursday on Thornbury Avenue, before being driven to nearby Manse Street, according to West Yorkshire Police.

Arfan Ali, 32, of Thornbury Avenue, is also charged with assault and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place. He is due to appear before Leeds magistrates later.

Councillor Ali remains in hospital in a serious but stable condition, police said.

Councillor Ali is a Your Bradford Independent Group representative for Bradford Moor ward and was first elected in May.

He works as a community development manager at charity The Leap, and was one of the founders of Leeds Road Festival.

articles.body: Days before Diljit Dosanjh's live concert at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, a Chandigarh-based academic has asked the singer to drop four songs from his setlist. He wants Diljit to leave all four out of the performance.Explaining his stand, he said, "These songs contain lyrics promoting alcohol, drugs and gun culture, which can have a negative impact on children. The Punjab and Haryana High Court had clearly directed in an order in my 2019 case that songs promoting alcohol, drugs and substance abuse should not be performed on stage. Despite this, Diljit Dosanjh performed these songs at concerts in Indore and Delhi."Reference to anti-drug campaignThe professor also pointed to the central government's anti-drug drive. He stated, "The country is running the Nasha Mukt Bharat campaign, with the government, public representatives, academics and others working to create awareness against drugs. It is wrong and illegal to promote such songs among children."He ended with a clear warning, "If he performs these songs, I will approach the Gujarat High Court and file a contempt of court case."Heavy security at the stadiumMeanwhile, Ahmedabad Police Commissioner Anupam Singh Gehlot has confirmed that elaborate arrangements are in place for the concert, with roughly 2,000 police personnel deputed to handle the crowd.Sharing the figures, Gehlot said, "Around 85,000 spectators and over 90,000 people, including support staff and security personnel, are expected to be present. 2,000 police personnel, three companies of the State Reserve Police, BDDS teams, Quick Response Teams, Crime Branch and SOG personnel have been deployed. DFMDs and door-frame metal detectors have been installed, while around 600 CCTV cameras will monitor the venue. Around 1,500 private security guards will also assist with entry, exit and internal arrangements."Traffic and entry rulesThe Commissioner added that steps have been taken to keep traffic flowing and ensure public safety. "Arrangements have been made to ensure smooth traffic and public safety. Items such as water bottles and bags are prohibited, while a locker facility will be available outside the venue. Women attendees will be allowed to carry small power banks," he said.Police have also set up surveillance, crowd-control and separate entry and exit systems to help fans move around easily. Canelo at 36 is still arguably the biggest draw in the sport. He recently returned to action for the first time since his defeat to Terence Crawford, where he comfortably beat Christian Mbilli to become the WBC super middleweight world champion. It remains to be seen what comes next for the Mexican , but his former promoter Oscar De La Hoya has spoken to Fight Hub TV, revealing his thoughts on Canelo's choice of opponents and impact on the sport.

Canelo Alvarez defeats Christian Mbilli to become world champion again

Alvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) entered the ring at The Venue in Riyadh as a challenger, and despite being out of the ring for over a year, the Mexican opted to challenge Mbilli for the world title.

The first few rounds were close, but Canelo's accuracy and experience soon shone through, as he won the majority of the rounds from the third round onwards. He picked his spots impressively and the accuracy from him seemed to make Mbilli reluctant to throw much in return.

When Mbilli did throw, Canelo often slipped the punch and countered effectively. Many expected the Cameroonian-born fighter to bring plenty of pressure, but he failed to do so. The scorecards read 117-110, 116-111, and 115-112, all in favour of Canelo, who was once again the WBC super middleweight champion.

After the fight, Canelo said: "I'm gonna rest. I'm gonna keep learning," Alvarez said. "I'm gonna keep working hard and right now I'm gonna take a couple of weeks off and then come back."

Whoever is next for Alvarez will be his fourth and final fight of the deal he has with Saudi Arabia's Turki Alalshikh. One person who is not convinced it will be a tough fight for Canelo is De La Hoya.

Oscar De La Hoya delivers verdict on Canelo Alvarez

Discussing Canelo's recent activity and his impact on boxing, De La Hoya said:

"Canelo's in the fourth quarter of his career, and he's picking fighters who he's gonna beat. That's the bottom line. Anybody who's next in line for Canelo, he's gonna beat. I don't wanna spend my hard-earned money watching Canelo just cruise by.

"Either get into a real fight, into a war, give us some action. I was literally falling asleep in the fight when I saw it in the replay. It was another snooze fest by him. I mean, how many times am I gonna see Canelo throw 100 punches a fight, when there's fighter's like William Zepeda throwing 100 punches a round?

"He's the face of boxing right now, but let's call it what it is, he's at the tail end of his career. He's milking the sport; he's milking the fans, making a lot of money. Good for him, but it doesn't do any good for the fans. It doesn't do any good for the sport of boxing to see him in these types of match-ups."

There's no doubting Canelo's influence on boxing is long-lasting, during the years in and around Covid-19, Canelo carried the sport, and put together a series of impressive performances. However, I can understand where De La Hoya is coming from. We all want to see him in the biggest fights possible, and the fact is that Mbilli is not that opponent.

As he was out of the ring for 13 months, I can understand this being his first fight back, and now that he has the WBC belt, unification fights could beckon, or could we see the Mexican go back up in weight and rematch Dmitry Bivol?

De La Hoya's views can be considered cloudy due to the previous lawsuit involving him and Canelo , and they have both made it clear their opinions of each other. There is clearly no love lost between De La Hoya and Canelo, but De La Hoya is right to a degree; aside from the Terence Crawford fight, the level of opponents has been underwhelming since then, and as Canelo moves towards the end of his career, we all want to see him involved in the biggest fights to solidify his legacy.
